problem.text: The commit addresses special-token omission while constructing the base decoded-piece vocabulary. Previously, the single-token decoding branch did not specify skip_special_tokens; the change explicitly passes False.

reasoning.text: This fixes vocabulary construction rather than changing the public decode API: retaining special-token text in the underlying table also makes it available to table consumers that do not request the extended special-token overlay.

impact.text: The change preserves vocabulary indexing and the list-of-strings interface, but can change strings observed by generation, reverse lookup, prefix matching and image-search token masks.

source_notes.text: The root loading-tokenization entry was read. It establishes the earlier design of eagerly cached piece tables and the whitespace-prefix probe on which this change relies.

PR #13, “Fix a tokenizer issue while converting models without a bos_token_id defined,” reports a different initialization failure. Issue #16, “RuntimeError: CUDA error: invalid configuration argument,” discusses tokenizer truncation during conversion. Their relationship to this task is only inferred from the shared tokenizer implementation; neither discussion establishes the motivation for this particular decode_batch change.

limitations: No real Hugging Face tokenizer or model was executed. The backend's version-specific default and special-token rendering behavior were not independently established.
The alternate whitespace-prefix branch still omits skip_special_tokens. The task therefore does not explicitly enforce special-token retention in both branches.
The bounded check uses an assumed backend default and synthetic token strings; it does not demonstrate checkpoint-specific output or generation behavior.

chapters.title: Retain special-token pieces in the base vocabulary

claims.text: get_fixed_vocab probes the encoding of ' t'. When that produces exactly one token whose decoded text has length two, it batch-decodes each vocabulary ID independently. The constants one and two describe this probe, not vocabulary-size or performance thresholds. Only this branch gains skip_special_tokens=False.

The alternate branch prepends the first token encoding a space, decodes each pair, then removes the decoded prefix length. That whitespace-preserving preparation remains unchanged, including its decode_batch arguments.

Whole-tree search finds get_id_to_piece_list as the sole direct caller of get_fixed_vocab. Initialization eagerly builds both piece-table variants and the reverse dictionary. The ordinary table takes the fixed vocabulary and appends extended IDs; the special variant copies it and overwrites entries from extended_id_to_piece. Consequently, an existing overlay can already supply a special spelling, whereas this edit repairs the underlying selected-branch decoding.

Inspected consumers remain structurally compatible: get_piece_to_id_dict reverses strings into IDs; prefix helpers inspect those strings; generation_loop indexes the ordinary table after checking stop conditions; imgsearch builds startswith masks; generator/job.py selects a table using decode_special_tokens and indexes it for output text. In particular, a False selection no longer guarantees empty special-token pieces in the changed branch. Public decode and decode_ are not modified.

A bounded check extracted get_fixed_vocab and applied the changed keyword against a stub backend assuming a True default. Its two-entry output changed from ['', ' t'] to ['<special>', ' t'], retaining length and position. This demonstrates argument propagation under that assumption, not actual backend decoding.

annotation.summary: Explicitly retains special-token text in one base-vocabulary decoding branch, affecting cached piece-table consumers without changing the public decode API.
